title: ROS Template v2 Data
description: Machine-readable payload for a v2-format (single prompt + short-form blocks) tokenized Run of Show template. Produced by pod-3A-ros-template-v2, consumed by pod-3B-client-ros at populate time. Distinct from the legacy ros-template.json shape - the two coexist and neither validates against the other. Freestanding by design: this file resolves no $ref outside its own directory and shares nothing with pod-3A-ros-template.
version_history: 1.0.0 - initial v2 schema (2026-08-14). Segment 1 as a block set with exactly one prompt; Segment 2 as per-city question blocks with a required per-question geo tag; 13-token placeholder inventory including YEARS_PRACTICING; region as plain text, never a token.

2.0.0 - format locked 2026-08-14. Added the `static` block carrying the 15 frozen boilerplate strings as schema-level constants; added `cover_page`; replaced segment_1's block set with the locked Introduction / attributes / internal_notes shape; removed `producer_notes` entirely (the section is gone from the format); Short-Form locations renamed from `cities` and pinned to exactly 10 questions; `geo_tag` retained as a generation record that is never rendered; `answer_note` removed.

2.0.1 - reconciled against the live reference implementation 2026-08-14: STATIC is 16 keys, not 15 (attr_note split into attr_note_internal + attr_sources_internal); added segment_1.attribute_sources; dropped `consistency` from attribute items since the counts moved below the divider.

2.0.2 - outro restructured 2026-08-18. The STATIC set is THREE strings (welcome, welcome_first, outro_note); the eleven constants retired 2026-08-17 and the four outro constants are no longer pinned here. outro_plug is gone in every form. The outro's three spoken lines moved to a generated `outro` block (thanks / signoff / reach) written against the beats and banks in references/outro-banks.json, in that order - the sign-off is deliberately not last. welcome now carries {{INTERVIEWER}}, matching references/statics.json and the twelve-token taxonomy in references/placeholders.md.

2.0.3 (2026-08-18) - placeholders_used enum reconciled to the twelve in references/placeholders.md. The prior 13-token enum lacked {{ATTORNEY}}, {{INTERVIEWER}} and {{TOPIC}}, every one of which appears in the welcome or the outro, so the outro's own tokens failed the placeholder gate.

2.1.0 (2026-08-18) - Short-Form bullets restored and Topic Plan provenance gated. Every S2 question now carries `bullets` (2 to 4, `[{Label}]{.underline}: {detail}`), required, after the restore documented in references/short-form.md. Every question also carries `topic_plan_ref`, required - a question with no ref is an invented question per gate TP-2. `q` is now the only accepted question field; the renderer's `question` fallback is dead and can be dropped. Added the top-level `metadata` block: `topic_plan_reconciled` is an enum of true and "legacy-exempt", and `topic_plan_doc_id`, `topic_plan_revision_id` and `topic_plan_fetched_at` are all required when it is true (gate TP-1). `cold_open`, `internal_notes` and `attribute_sources` dropped out of segment_1.required - all three are retired per references/document-structure.md, and all three are still written by scripts/build-ros-template-v2-docx.py, so the properties stay defined rather than deleted until the renderer stops emitting them. Stale descriptions on `questions` ("bare bullets ... with nothing else per question") and `segment_2` ("the two mode notes come from STATIC") rewritten. placeholders_used and the static block verified against references/placeholders.md and references/statics.json - both already correct, no change.

2.1.1 (2026-08-18) - re-pinned the three static consts against references/statics.json. The welcome const still carried the pre-shrink value that merged Introduction lines 1 and 2; statics.json had already been shrunk to line 1 only, so every real payload failed the STATIC gate.
2.1.2 (2026-08-18) - added segment_1.setup as the canonical name for Introduction line 2; cold_open kept as a deprecated alias.

2.2.0 (2026-08-18) - {{RECORDING_DATE}} retired from the taxonomy. Enum drops to eleven tokens and cover_page.recording_date_token is removed. A ROS Template is generic and reusable across every firm that records the episode, so a recording date was never a template-level fact.

2.3.0 (2026-08-18) - added segment_1.credential as Introduction line 3. It was previously folded into `prompt`, which rendered the credential and the ask as one run-on paragraph. references/introduction.md always specified them as separate lines.

2.4.0 (2026-08-18) - drift sweep. segment_1.description rewritten to the four-line Introduction (welcome / setup / credential / prompt); topic_phrase no longer described as a substitution into welcome; the static block, welcome and welcome_first descriptions corrected to say NOTHING substitutes into a constant; outro_close.description drops the INTERVIEWER speaker tag, cut 2026-08-18 per gate OC-1. Descriptions only - no shape, enum, const or required change, so every payload that validated against 2.3.0 still validates.

2.5.0 (2026-08-26) - welcome and welcome_first change from const to a two-value enum: the standard string, or the embedded-name variant for podcast names that embed the attorney's name (e.g. 'Car Accident Attorney w. Robert May'), where 'with **{{ATTORNEY_NAME}}**' would double the name (Gabe, 2026-08-26). A 'w.' in the podcast name is spoken, and rendered in the welcome, as 'with'. Every payload valid against 2.4.0 stays valid.

2.5.1 (2026-08-26, locked) - descriptions only. Line 1 precedence locked per Gabe: a podcast name of the shape '{Prefix} w./with {Attorney}' renders the SPLIT SPOKEN form at populate ('Welcome back to the {Prefix} podcast with {Attorney}.', plain text, no bolds) - computed by pod-3B-client-ros-v2, so it never appears in this TEMPLATE payload; the enum's embedded value is the fallback for names with no 'w./with' splice point. See references/statics.json -> welcome_split_rule.

schema_version.description: The FORMAT generation, not this file's revision. v2 payloads carry 2.0.0 and keep carrying it; the file's own revision is the `version` field above. Bumping this const rejects every payload already in flight, so it moves only when the payload shape breaks compatibility.

episode_format.description: Hard-pinned. A legacy-segments template does not validate against this schema and must use pod-3A-ros-template instead.

location.description: Required when scope is Location or Extension. Format CA, CA - Los Angeles County, CA - Long Beach. No colons; dashes only. This is the Episode geo target, which may differ from the show-wide Optimization scope (show anchor).

city.description: The Episode geo target city that {{CITY}} resolves to at populate time. Null at Topic Only scope.

region.description: PLAIN TEXT region the city is paired with in Segment 2, e.g. 'Chatham County and coastal Georgia'. Fixed by this template's location scope. NEVER a placeholder - {{REGION}} does not exist. Null at Topic Only scope.

state.description: Full state name, used by STATE-tagged questions.

duration.description: Segment 1 is ALWAYS a range, never a single figure, and never carries per-question budgets.

segment_1.description: S1: Long-Form. A four-line Introduction - STATIC welcome (line 1), generated `setup` (line 2), generated `credential` (line 3, its own paragraph), then exactly one generated credential-led `prompt` (line 4, the only bolded prompt) - followed by the attribute bullets under ATTORNEY RESPONSE. The outro closes S1. `cold_open`, `internal_notes` and `attribute_sources` are RETIRED per references/document-structure.md and are no longer required; they remain defined only because scripts/build-ros-template-v2-docx.py still renders all three.

topic_phrase.description: GENERATED. The episode subject as a plain phrase. It feeds the `setup` line's subject slot and the outro's topical credit approach. It is NOT substituted into any STATIC string - it left `welcome` on 2026-08-18 when that constant shrank to Introduction line 1.

cold_open.description: DEPRECATED alias for setup, kept so older payloads still validate. Emit `setup`.

prompt.description: GENERATED. EXACTLY ONE credential-led prompt, rendered in full bold.

attributes.description: Rendered as name plus plain-language detail only, with no `Attributes to Hit` heading (retired 2026-08-17). Gate AT-2 in references/attributes.md wants TEN to TWELVE bullets; minItems stays at 5 here so the count stays a gate rather than a hard schema reject. Zero question marks anywhere in the block (AT-1).

internal_notes.description: RETIRED 2026-08-17 - references/document-structure.md lists 'Internal Notes (not read on air) and everything under it' under 'Retired - must not come back'. No longer required on segment_1. NOT deleted because scripts/build-ros-template-v2-docx.py still reads s1['internal_notes'], inotes['examples'] and inotes['need_to_know'] unguarded. When present the inner shape is still enforced so a half-populated block fails loudly rather than at render time.

need_to_know.description: GENERATED. Plain-language coverage bullets, jargon-free per Editorial Guideline 3.

attribute_sources.description: RETIRED 2026-08-17 with the rest of the Internal Notes block - the source-consistency counts are named explicitly in references/document-structure.md -> 'Retired - must not come back', and references/attributes.md rule 'No source counts on the page'. Optional. NOT deleted because scripts/build-ros-template-v2-docx.py still iterates s1.get('attribute_sources', []) and renders a bullet per entry. Provenance belongs in metadata.

setup.description: Introduction line 2, GENERATED. One of the ten line-2 patterns in references/introduction.md. Renamed from cold_open on 2026-08-18 when statics.json -> welcome was shrunk to line 1 only and this stopped being a cold open in any sense.

credential.description: Introduction line 3, GENERATED. One credential frame, ending with the turn toward the attorney. Its own paragraph: the ask in line 4 lands as a turn only if line 3 fully stops first. Placeholders carry bold; the line is not bold in full, so `prompt` remains the single bolded prompt the gate asserts.

follow_ups.description: Interviewer notes rendered under the S1 attribute block. The first bullet is hard-coded by the renderer; these are the topic-specific ones, and at least one must prompt the attorney for a case study. Never read on air, never a question.

segment_2.description: S2: Short-Form (60-90s). Follows the S1 outro after a horizontal divider - it no longer starts its own page, and only the Appendix still does. One block per location, each exactly ten questions, each question carrying two to four attorney bullets. The two short-form mode notes that used to head the section were retired 2026-08-17 and are not in the STATIC set; the only line above the blocks is the shipped 60-to-90-second direction note held in the renderer.

questions.description: EXACTLY ten. Hard cap, not a range. Each renders as `**Q{N}: {q}**` - the question is bold IN FULL, `Q{N}:` label included - followed by its two to four attorney bullets. Nothing else renders under a question: no time budget, no geo tag line, no source ref, no answer-guidance note (SF-4). The ten hold the live Topic Plan Doc's relative order; tail truncation is allowed, reordering and mid-sequence gaps are not (TP-3).

q.description: THE question field. Phrased as a search, not a legal element. `question` is NOT accepted - the renderer's `q or question` fallback in scripts/build-ros-template-v2-docx.py and scripts/verify-topic-plan.py is dead once this is required, and should be dropped. Carries no `**` markers of its own; the whole line renders bold and a nested marker unbolds the token it wraps.

bullets.description: The attorney bullets, restored 2026-08-18 (references/short-form.md -> 'Why the bullets came back'). Two to four, three the default - a 60 to 90 second answer has no room for six. Each renders as `[{Label}]{.underline}: {detail}`: the label is two or three words, UNDERLINED and never bold, as pandoc and never HTML `<u>`, so the question keeps the only bold weight in the block. The detail is one clause or one short sentence saying WHAT TO COVER, never a question (SF-3), plain language and zero jargon. The object form is canonical. A preformatted string is also accepted because scripts/build-ros-template-v2-docx.py -> sf_bullets() passes one through untouched and steps/05-segment-2.md still declares `bullets: [str]`; drop the string branch here once that step emits objects.

label.description: Two or three words. Rendered underlined, never bold. No trailing colon - the renderer adds it.

detail.description: One clause or one short sentence. What to cover, never a question.

oneOf.description: LEGACY passthrough. An already-formatted `[{Label}]{.underline}: {detail}` string. Accepted only because the renderer accepts it; new payloads emit the object form.

topic_plan_ref.description: REQUIRED, never null. Points at the row in the LIVE Topic Plan Google Doc this question derives from. A question with no ref is an invented question and fails gate TP-2 in references/short-form.md. Local topic-plan-v{n}.json / .md mirrors do not count - clients edit and veto in the Doc by hand and none of it propagates back.

geo_tag.description: Generation record only - NEVER rendered. Exactly one per question; the schema enforces the vocabulary, gate SF-5 enforces the distribution (exactly three CITY-tagged per location, across exactly ten questions). The pod-2B city-share ceiling is NOT applied here.

source_ngram_ref.description: Null allowed ONLY when kind is attribute.

appendix_question_bank.description: EVERY n-gram table row, verbatim and unedited, renumbered 1..M. Audit trail and pull pool. INTERNAL - stripped by pod-3B-client-ros. Still starts its own page; S2 no longer does.

placeholders_used.description: The approved token taxonomy, ELEVEN tokens. VERIFIED byte-for-byte against references/placeholders.md on 2026-08-18 - the table there and this enum match exactly, no change needed. {{ATTORNEY_FIRST_NAME}}, {{HOST_NAME}} and {{PRACTICE_AREA}} were retired for {{ATTORNEY}}, {{INTERVIEWER}} and {{TOPIC}}; {{EPISODE_NUMBER}} left the rendered body and survives only in filenames. {{REGION}} does not exist and must never be invented - it was invented twice and removed twice.

static.description: The three frozen boilerplate strings, verbatim from references/statics.json -> strings. VERIFIED byte-for-byte against that file on 2026-08-18 - all three consts match, no change needed. Byte-identical on every episode, client and scope. Never regenerated. NOTHING substitutes into any of them as of 2026-08-18, when {topic_phrase} moved out of `welcome`. Any substitution on a string carrying tokens is .replace() never .format() - str.format collapses the doubled braces and silently destroys every token. The outro's three spoken lines are NOT here; they are generated per episode against references/outro-banks.json. Eleven further constants were retired 2026-08-17 and are preserved in references/statics.json -> retired.

welcome.description: Introduction line 1, every episode after the first. The sonic marker, and nothing else - the setup that used to ride along in this string is now the generated `segment_1.setup`. No substitution. The second value is the embedded-name FALLBACK (Gabe, 2026-08-26, locked): podcast names that embed the attorney's name never append 'with **{{ATTORNEY_NAME}}**', which would double the name - and a name of the shape '{Prefix} w./with {Attorney}' takes the computed SPLIT SPOKEN form at populate instead (statics.json -> welcome_split_rule), which never appears in this template payload.

welcome_first.description: Introduction line 1, episode 1 only - the launch episode. There is no 'back' to welcome anyone to yet. Same shrink as `welcome`: line 1 only, no substitution. Second value is the embedded-name variant (Gabe, 2026-08-26).

cover_page.description: Branded cover block, built to the CE deliverable cover spec (see SKILL.md Editorial Guideline 4). The logo is inserted as a separate API call after the text batch; the cover page gate checks the inline object actually landed.

outro_close.description: The STATIC outro_note, then the three generated lines in order: thanks, sign-off, reach-out. No speaker tag - the INTERVIEWER tag was cut 2026-08-18, since outro_note already says who is speaking (gate OC-1). The sign-off is deliberately not last - the reach-out lands after it as a tag. Carries no fields of its own; every rendered value comes from `static.outro_note` and the `outro` block.

outro.description: The three spoken outro lines. NOT constants as of 2026-08-18 - Gabe required the outro to read unique per episode, so each line is GENERATED against the required beats, invariants and banks in references/outro-banks.json. The banks are starting points showing range, not closed menus. Only outro_note remains STATIC, and it is host direction rather than spoken. Rotation across a client's library is enforced per references/outro-banks.json -> rotation; the run records outro_line1_approach, outro_line1_stem_index, outro_line2_index and outro_line3_slots in metadata. Gates live in references/outro.md.

thanks.description: Line 1. Addresses {{ATTORNEY}} exactly once in bold, thanks them explicitly, and carries one credit clause that alludes to competence rather than announcing it. Under 30 words. Never a superlative, a ranking, or an award.

signoff.description: Line 2. Signals the end, names {{PODCAST_NAME}} exactly once in bold, and points forward to a next episode. Under 15 words. Variation is LOW by design - this is the sonic bookend to intro line 1. Zero occurrences of Case Engine, no episode number, no next-episode tease.

reach.description: Line 3, the tag AFTER the sign-off. Hinge opener, a geo qualifier carrying {{STATE}}, a practice-area-neutral need clause, then {{FIRM_NAME}}, {{PHONE_NUMBER}} and {{WEBSITE}}, each exactly once and all bold. Under 30 words. Zero occurrences of {{CITY}} - S1 is state-governed so one recording serves every city the firm covers.

metadata.description: Run provenance. Mirrors metadata.json; scripts/verify-topic-plan.py reads payload['metadata'] and falls back to the payload root. Open by design - the run also records the outro rotation fields (outro_line1_approach, outro_line1_stem_index, outro_line2_index, outro_line3_slots) and the attribute provenance (attribute_source, its pull date and confidence) here, so unlisted keys are allowed.

topic_plan_reconciled.description: Gate SF-9. `true` means the live Topic Plan Doc was fetched and reconciled this run. `"legacy-exempt"` means the plan predates the requirement and is not retrofitted - claiming it on a newly generated plan is the exact failure this field exists to make visible. There is no third value: `false` and a missing field both FAIL.

topic_plan_doc_id.description: The PUBLISHED Topic Plan Google Doc. The only authority - a run built from a local topic-plan-v{n} mirror alone FAILS (TP-1).

topic_plan_revision_id.description: The Doc's revisionId at fetch time. Proves WHICH version of the client's edits this build reconciled against.

topic_plan_fetched_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the live fetch, this run.

outro_line1_approach.description: Rotation record, gate OC-7. May not repeat within two episodes.

outro_line2_index.description: Rotation record. A bank entry may not repeat within two episodes.

outro_line3_slots.description: The four chosen slots: hinge, geo-and-need, verb, contact frame. Must differ from the preceding episode in at least two.

attribute_source.description: Gate AT-8. `fallback` is Inferred, never Confirmed, and carries its pull date.

attribute_source_pulled.description: Pull date of the attribute set, required in spirit whenever attribute_source is `fallback`.
